newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 15.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* DLJ posted a record $100.2 million profit for the second quarter.
* The dollar hit a six-year high against the mark.
* The Nasdaq composite rose 21.26 to 1523.88, its eighth straight record.
* Raytheon agreed to sell part of its appliance unit for $550 million.
* The DuPont plan to buy some industrial chemical businesses from ICI for $3 billion had analysts wondering how DuPont will squeeze profits from the businesses.
* Marriott International said it has curtailed an effort to target more disadvantaged welfare recipients in its successful welfare-to-work program.
* Texaco 's inquiry into charges growing out of a race-bias suit sound three officials purposefully failed to turn over evidence.
* The port of Los Angeles is facing the possibility of serious labor disruptions as striking harbor pilots triggered sympathy work stoppage among dockworkers.
* White House officials plan a meeting with cigarette makers today to question the penalties the industry would pay if youth smoking persists under the proposed tobacco pact.
* Colgate-Polmolive won FDA approval to market Total toothpaste in the U.S., making it the only toothpaste that can legitimately advertise that it helps prevent gum disease.
* A nasal-spray vaccine developed by Aviron prevented the flu in a large test.
* NationsBank and other banks posted earnings that met or beat analyst's expectations.
* LTV said it would close a major coke-producing plant by the end of the yearand take a $150 millio charge.
* Allinace Entertainment filed for bankruptcy protection.
* Though many analysts praised the idea of NationsBank buying Montgomery Securities, some questioned the rich price.
* Bond prices declined moderately as investors awaited a government report today on June retail sales.
